settings.eyebrow: The hidden cost of the wrong pillow
settings.heading: Most pillows collapse. Your neck pays the price.
settings.text: Soft pillows flatten within minutes and pull your head out of line with your spine. Over 7–8 hours a night, that strain can show up as:

settings.title: Morning stiffness
settings.text: Waking up needing to “crack” your neck before the day starts.

settings.title: Tension headaches
settings.text: Neck muscles bracing all night can leave tension in the morning.

settings.title: Shoulder & upper-back strain
settings.text: A collapsed pillow lets your shoulder take the weight on its own.

settings.title: Cooling-tech cover
settings.text: Breathable, removable and machine-washable. OEKO-TEX® certified, in black with white side panels.

settings.title: High-density adaptive memory foam
settings.text: Pure white, uniform foam that softens to your shape with body heat and pressure, then holds that shape.

settings.title: Dual-height contour profile
settings.text: A higher neck roll for side sleepers and a lower one for back sleepers, both shaped to keep the cervical curve supported.

settings.label: Side sleeper
settings.text: The higher side fills the space between your shoulder and ear, so your head doesn't drop toward the mattress. Your nose should line up with the centre of your chest.

settings.label: Back sleeper
settings.text: The lower roll supports the curve behind your neck while the centre cradles your head, so your chin doesn't tuck toward your chest.

settings.label: Stomach sleeper
settings.text: We'll be honest: stomach sleeping twists your neck to one side for hours, and no pillow can fully correct that. Many people use Pilo to retrain themselves into side sleeping.

settings.eyebrow: Designed with spinal health in mind
settings.heading: A sleep tool, not just a soft place to land.
settings.text: Pilo puts structure and support first. Softness comes second.

settings.title: Neutral alignment
settings.text: The contour is shaped to keep your head, neck and upper spine in one line.

settings.title: Won't bottom out
settings.text: The high-density core resists flattening night after night.

settings.title: Cooling cover
settings.text: Breathable fabric that helps manage heat through humid summers.

settings.heading: Sleep on it for 30 nights. Literally.
settings.text: Your neck needs a few nights to adapt. If Pilo isn't right for you after 30 nights, we'll arrange a pickup.

settings.question: Is it normal for Pilo to feel firm or strange at first?
settings.answer: Yes. Your neck has adapted to years of unsupported sleep. Most people need 3–7 nights to adjust to an ergonomic pillow, and you may notice your neck muscles as they adapt to a neutral position. Give it at least a week; that's why every Pilo comes with a 30-night trial.

settings.question: Which side of the pillow should I use?
settings.answer:
Side sleepers: use the higher side. It fills the gap between your shoulder and ear.
Back sleepers: use the lower side. Your chin shouldn't tilt toward your chest, and your head shouldn't tip back.

settings.question: Will Pilo fix my neck pain?
settings.answer: Pilo is designed to support healthy cervical alignment while you sleep, which many people find reduces morning stiffness. It is not a medical device or treatment. If you have persistent or severe pain, please consult a doctor or physiotherapist.

settings.question: Is there a smell when I open it?
settings.answer: New memory foam can have a light, harmless “new” scent for 24–48 hours. Remove the packaging and let it air in a ventilated room.

settings.question: Will it make me hot?
settings.answer: The cover uses a breathable cooling fabric, made with Lebanon's humid summers in mind.

settings.question: How do I wash it?
settings.answer: Unzip and machine-wash the cover only on a cold (30°C max), gentle cycle, then air dry. Do not wash or soak the foam. Spot-clean it with a damp cloth and keep it away from direct sun and heaters.
